subject.title: [Feature]: Track data provenance across session boundaries for persistent state

question: Should OpenClaw add a core/plugin-API provenance chain for durable state writes and reads, and which session/tool/origin metadata may be persisted and exposed to plugins?
rationale: The remaining work defines security boundaries, public Plugin SDK contracts, persisted schema, migration behavior, and read-time trust policy, so automation cannot choose the permanent API shape safely.

options.title: Design Minimal Provenance API First
options.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer/security design that specifies metadata, plugin visibility, migration behavior, and read-time policy before implementation.

options.title: Split Into Hook Prerequisites
options.body: Use the open before_tool_call and before_persistence_write proposals as prerequisite API work, then return to the durable provenance chain after those contracts settle.

options.title: Defer To Memory Plugin Contracts
options.body: Decide that provenance stays in memory/plugin-specific layers for now unless a concrete missing core API is proven by an implementation.

recommendation.title: Design Minimal Provenance API First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer/security design that specifies metadata, plugin visibility, migration behavior, and read-time policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The inter-session provenance history and product/security boundary make steipete the best available routing candidate from the code-history set.
